doc: ONLY THE 4 NEAREST ARE QUERIED. On this draw the texel (row 6, col 47) is covered by a 5th-nearest lump whose dome is 0.066 higher than the best of the 4 nearest: Python IGNORES it (k = 4), so a port that scans every lump covering a texel (a 3x3 cell neighborhood, k = 5 or more) differs there and nowhere else on this tile (about 2 texels in 4 million do). The texel (row 37, col 10) is won by the 4th-nearest lump (a max over 3 is lower by 0.115). The jittered lump grid (60 x 60 = 3600 centers g, [x, y] in tile units, and their radii r (0.35 to 0.7 of the spacing)) is the input (plan0.g, plan0.r); freq = round(240 / 4) = 60 is read from the source (params.constants). dome = max over the 4 NEAREST lumps (by distance, periodic KD tree, not by normalized distance) of clip(1 - dist / r, 0, 1)^0.6. Measured: every random input nudged by one float64 ulp (8 trials) and numpy.fft replaced by scipy.fft: max |diff| 6e-14, because x^0.6 has an infinite slope at 0 (a distance within an ulp of r moves the value by up to (1e-16)^0.6 = 1.6e-10): 1e-9 relative, 1e-9 absolute.
